The scalar quadratic has exactly one root y_- in (0,1) and y_+>1; y_- crosses r=rho^q once. The q inverse images are distinct and simple for t>T; equality roots lie on |z|=1. My independent SymPy simplification verified g(r)/(q-g(r)L)=T_q(rho) identically, including critical normalization. As t increases without bound y_-->r^2 and the roots approach rho times qth roots of unity; asymptotic limits follow from exact formula. No claim concerns K_t(z,z).
